r0.why: Definition with non-zero integer polynomial [1]; rational coefficients equivalent via least common denominator [26][27]; golden ratio root of x^2-x-1 [2].

r1.why: Integers, rationals, n-th roots algebraic [3]; a/b root of bx-a [9]; sqrt2 and cbrt3/2 polynomials [23]; 1+i root of x^4+4 [2]; Gaussian integers and their quadratic [12][13].

r2.why: Unique monic minimal polynomial of least degree [28][29]; monic means a=1 [11]; degree n [30]; rationals degree 1, degree 2 quadratic irrationals [31]; cosines and irreducible cubic, conjugates [19][20].

r3.why: Closed under four operations, field Q-bar [4]; real algebraic numbers a field [5]; radical expressions algebraic [16]; algebraically closed [43][44]; smallest such field, algebraic closure [45].

r4.why: Roots of x^5-x+1 not expressible by arithmetic and n-th roots [17], algebraic by definition [1]; many but not all degree 5+ polynomials [18].

r5.why: Transcendental incl. pi and e [6][25]; countable, measure 0, no space [34]; almost all transcendental [7][35]; dense in reals via rationals [32][33].
